donors.reason: Indolecarboxamide EZH2 inhibitor class; highest anchor and structure similarity to GSK126, likely transfers H3K27me3 loss.
Thienopyrimidine N-arylpiperazine; high anchor similarity but no EZH2 mechanism described, so histone transfer uncertain.

revised_hypotheses: GSK126 at 1 uM for 24 h in A375 is expected to inhibit EZH2 and reduce H3K27me3, giving a reproducible histone perturbation >0.5 log2 versus vehicle.
CPI-169 (BRD-A48881734) is the best-supported donor because it is an indolecarboxamide EZH2 inhibitor with high anchor and structure similarity to GSK126.
BRD-K90860366 has high anchor similarity but its retrieved description lacks EZH2 inhibition, so it is a weaker mechanistic donor for H3K27me3 loss.
unresolved: No measured histone response values are supplied for any donor, so transfer of a >0.5 log2 H3K27me3 perturbation cannot be verified.
Verapamil, Regorafenib, and Ibrutinib have retrieved descriptions but no EZH2-related mechanism, so they are not supported as histone-mark donors.
The specific target cell, feature, and sign for the external decoder transfer remain unspecified.
